relationships.description: The $ref usage site is traced to the application service whose operations accept or return instances of the type it points at, linking a reused data shape to the behavior that handles it.
relationships.evidence: A mapping annotation on the $ref node (e.g. an x-service extension) or a traceability document names the application service, and that service's operation signatures use the type the $ref resolves to.

relationships.description: The $ref pointer in the data model corresponds to an OpenAPI schema, so the value it delegates to is exchanged over the API with the shape that API schema defines.
relationships.evidence: The OpenAPI document contains a matching $ref (e.g. '#/components/schemas/Address') or an inline schema generated from or resolving to the same JSON Schema definition, as shown by a code-generation config or a shared schema file.

relationships.description: The $ref usage site points at the named reusable definition, which supplies all the validation rules applied to instances at that position.
relationships.evidence: The $ref value (e.g. '#/definitions/Address') resolves through JSON Pointer evaluation to an existing entry under the document's 'definitions' keyword with that name.

notes: maps-to application.applicationservice looks misplaced: a $ref adds no content of its own, so any service mapping belongs on the SchemaDefinition it resolves to. The same applies, less strongly, to maps-to api.schema, which duplicates what the resolved definition would map to.
